crowdsourced_ai_results.analysis: The provided sample is a 64-bit Windows kernel-mode driver that implements a standard Kernel Streaming (KS) filter, specifically identified as a 'WDM Tee/Communication Transform Filter'. The binary utilizes the AVStream framework, importing legitimate functions from the Windows Kernel Streaming library (ks.sys) such as KsInitializeDriver, KsFilterGetFirstChildPin, and KsPinGetConnectedPinInterface. Analysis of the 'PinCreate' and 'FilterProcess' functions shows standard handling of stream property sets (KSPROPSETID_Connection, KSPROPSETID_StreamInterface) and data buffer propagation typical of a Tee filter, which splits or transforms media streams. The use of the 'MSTE' (Microsoft Tee) pool tag further confirms its identity as a standard multimedia component. No malicious behaviors or suspicious IOCs were identified.
